assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: Methods like appliesFragileSurcharge use 'boolean fragile' column and set options via options.setFragile(fragile), not a map column. appliesInsurancePremium uses 'BigDecimal insuredValue' column, not a map. appliesHazmatHandlingFee uses 'String handling' column, not a map.

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method is present in the test class. Options are constructed manually via 'new PackageOptions()' and setter calls, not via a converter from a map column.

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Tables use 'Dimensions' column with list values like '[10, 10, 10]', '[70, 50, 10]', '[100, 5, 5]', '[101, 5, 5]' and method parameter 'List<Integer> dimensions'.

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Eight separate @TableTest methods: calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight, appliesDimensionalWeightWhenGreaterThanActual, appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit, appliesFragileSurcharge, appliesInsurancePremiumWithMinimum, appliesHazmatHandlingFee, combinesSurchargesInOrder, carrierDoesNotAffectPrice.

assertions.text: Parameter types correspond to the ShippingCostCalculator.calculateShippingCost interface — weight, cost, and dimension types match the method signature.
assertions.evidence: Methods use 'double weight', 'List<Integer> dimensions', 'BigDecimal' for costs, and 'Carrier carrier' enum. Results compared via 'expected.compareTo(actual)' for BigDecimal.

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenario column uses descriptive names: 'EU standard, light', 'EU express, medium', 'Small package, actual weight used', 'Large package, dimensional weight used', 'Fragile and insured', 'Same zone and weight, any carrier'.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Base Rate?, Rate?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?

assertions.text: Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: Tables use 'Region', 'Speed', 'Weight', 'Fragile', 'Handling', 'Insured Value', 'Carrier' as separate columns instead of a single 'Options' map column. No 'Options' column present; options are threaded as individual boolean/string/BigDecimal parameters.

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 8 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: Output contains no TestNG syntax: no @DataProvider, @Test(dataProvider=...), Object[][], or TestNG imports (org.testng.*).
